Control settings for Hager-Zhang line search

Source: R/hager_zhang.R
HagerZhangControl.Rd

Tuning parameters for the Hager-Zhang line-search implementation.

Usage

HagerZhangControl(
  delta = 0.1,
  sigma = 0.9,
  alphamax = Inf,
  rho = 5,
  epsilon = 1e-06,
  gamma = 0.66,
  linesearchmax = 50,
  psi3 = 0.1,
  c = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

delta

Sufficient decrease constant (Wolfe condition 1). Must satisfy 0 < delta < sigma < 1. Smaller values accept shorter steps more readily.

sigma

Curvature condition constant (Wolfe condition 2). This line search constant is unrelated to the sigma parameters of the measurement and conductance models. Must satisfy delta < sigma < 1. Values close to 1 relax the curvature requirement and allow fewer function evaluations per step.

alphamax

Upper bound on the trial step length. The default Inf lets the bracketing phase grow the step without limit.

rho

Multiplicative expansion factor applied during the initial bracketing phase. Must be > 1.

epsilon

Non-negative tolerance defining an "approximate Wolfe" regime near a local minimum: a small positive value (default 1e-6) allows the algorithm to accept a slightly increased objective near convergence.

gamma

Minimum fractional reduction of the bracket required after each secant step. Steps that shrink by less than this factor trigger bisection instead. Must be in (0, 1).

linesearchmax

Maximum number of line-search function evaluations. Raise this if the optimizer reports repeated line-search failures on difficult problems.

psi3

Backtracking multiplier applied when the initial trial step produces a non-finite objective. Must be in (0, 1).

c

Initial trial step length passed to the line search. The default 1.0 is appropriate for Newton and quasi-Newton methods that produce unit-scale search directions.

verbose

Should line-search progress (trial step lengths and objective values) be printed to the console?

Value

A named list of class "terradish_hager_zhang_control" holding the line search settings. The elements are the arguments above, stored unchanged: delta, sigma, alphamax, rho, epsilon, gamma, linesearchmax, psi3, c, and verbose. Pass the object to the ls.control argument of NewtonRaphsonControl rather than to terradish directly; inspect it with str(). The list carries no fitted quantities, so nothing in it needs back-transforming.

Details

HagerZhangControl() is the default line search used by NewtonRaphsonControl. It implements the approximate Wolfe conditions from Hager and Zhang (2006), which combine sufficient-decrease and curvature checks with a bracketing-plus-secant strategy.

The default parameters work well for most resistance-surface optimization problems. Common reasons to change them:

  • Line-search failures: increase linesearchmax or loosen sigma toward 1.

  • Slow convergence with many small steps: tighten sigma (e.g. 0.5; it must stay above delta) to enforce a stronger curvature condition.

  • Initial non-finite objectives: increase psi3 to take larger backtracking steps when c is too large.

References

Hager WW, Zhang H. 2006. Algorithm 851: CG_DESCENT, a conjugate gradient method with guaranteed descent. ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 32(1):113-137. doi:10.1145/1132973.1132979 .

See also

NewtonRaphsonControl, ArmijoControl

Other optimizer controls: ArmijoControl(), NewtonRaphsonControl()

Examples

ctrl <- HagerZhangControl(verbose = FALSE, linesearchmax = 10)
str(ctrl)
#> List of 10
#>  $ delta        : num 0.1
#>  $ sigma        : num 0.9
#>  $ alphamax     : num Inf
#>  $ rho          : num 5
#>  $ epsilon      : num 1e-06
#>  $ gamma        : num 0.66
#>  $ linesearchmax: num 10
#>  $ psi3         : num 0.1
#>  $ c            : num 1
#>  $ verbose      : logi FALSE
#>  - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "terradish_hager_zhang_control" "list"

# Use inside NewtonRaphsonControl:
opt_ctrl <- NewtonRaphsonControl(
  maxit = 50,
  ls.control = HagerZhangControl(sigma = 0.5, linesearchmax = 30)
)
